people.jesus.role: Son of the Father, our Counselor and the atoning sacrifice
people.jesus.relations: The writer joins fellowship with the Father to fellowship with his Son, Jesus Christ.
people.jesus.meaning: The writers say they heard, saw, and touched the Word of life. His blood cleanses us from all sin. He is a Counselor with the Father and the atoning sacrifice for our sins. He laid down his life for us. Believers should also lay down their lives for the brothers.
people.cain.relations: The letter sets his evil deeds beside the righteous deeds of his brother.
people.cain.meaning: The writer says to love one another, unlike Cain. Cain was of the evil one and killed his brother. The writer says his deeds were evil and his brother’s righteous. Whoever hates his brother is called a murderer.
sources.web.summary: The full text of First John is the main text for the close readings.
sources.web.limits: The speaker is unnamed. Authorship, dates, Greek forms, manuscripts, and the audience’s situation were not checked independently. The identity of the opponents who left was not checked either. The text names no city and no modern opponent.
sources.cfm-nt-2023-49.summary: The lesson links God’s light and love to conduct and to staying in Christ’s teaching.
sources.cfm-nt-2023-49.limits: For First John, the lesson covers all five chapters. Linked Restoration texts, hymns, and reference entries were not reviewed independently. The lesson’s use of apostasy is Church teaching.
sources.ok-john.summary: Ok links practical love to meeting the material needs of fellow believers.
sources.ok-john.limits: This is Ok’s own reading. Her Greek word study and claims about unusual wording were not checked independently. Her modern examples were not checked either. The audience’s situation is not described here.
